newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SUPER 12 SETS NEW STANDARDS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SUPER 12 SETS NEW STANDARDS.

text.p: The first weekend of the 1997 Super 12 allayed any fears that the southern hemisphere's premier provincial tournament might not live up to the reputation it earned last year.

Johannesburg's Sunday Times said Auckland's 40-40 draw against Northern Transvaal, "will go down as one of the greatest games ever played at Loftus Versfeld", while the Sunday Independent called it "one to cherish...a match of sublime quality".

Northerns tied the scores with a try in the last minute and Auckland captain Sean Fitzpatrick said: "We're obviously disappointed not to take away maximum points, but it was a great game to play in and I rate this stadium the best in the world."
The encounter at Loftus was the jewel in the crown of the first four fixtures, but there was much to admire in the other three, all of which finished with no more than five points between the teams.

The ACT Brumbies gave notice that Australia has three genuine final prospects by beating Queensland 24-19 in Brisbane. The Brumbies scored three brilliant tries and ran up a 24-7 lead before Wallaby star Tim Horan earned a consolation point for his tem with two late tries.
It was a similar story in New Zealand where Waikato, boosted by a number of North Harbour stars won a tense encounter against Wellington 23-18.
The scores were level at 18-18 in the 68th minute when All Black centre Frank Bunce chipped over the Wellington defence to put in fellow All Black Glenn Osborne for the winning score.
In the final encounter of the weekend as Transvaal defeated Free State 24-20 in Bloemfontein.
Without their captain of the last five years, Francois Pienaar, Transvaal struggled for fluency and were particularly short of back row ideas.
But the vagaries of the modern game were highlighted by the fact that Free State scrummed Transvaal into the ground and still could not win at home.

In the circumstances the Cheetahs will not be looking forward to Friday night's visit from Auckland, while Northern Transvaal will face Queensland at Loftus with fresh determination after their classic show of pride on Saturday.
